name: Corvus Blackwood
equipment: A stolen fey trinket (a tiny music box that plays a tune from Wonderland — the object that drew him here)
A raven feather quill (his familiar's feather)
features: Infernal Legacy (thaumaturgy cantrip; hellish rebuke 1/day as 2nd-level spell at level 3; darkness 1/day at level 5)
Expertise (Stealth, Thieves' Tools — double proficiency bonus)
Sneak Attack (3d6 — once per turn, extra damage when you have advantage or ally is within 5 ft.)
Cunning Action (bonus action to Dash, Disengage, or Hide)
Uncanny Dodge (use reaction to halve an attack's damage against you)
Mage Hand Legerdemain (invisible Mage Hand, can stow/retrieve objects, pick locks, disarm traps at range, bonus action to control)
Spellcasting (Arcane Trickster — INT-based, enchantment and illusion spells)
False Identity (Charlatan feature — established a second identity with documentation, disguises, and established contacts)

personality.traits: I lie as easily as I breathe and I'm not always sure which is which anymore. I name every object I own and talk to my raven familiar 'Poe' as though he's the only person whose opinion I respect. I collect shiny things compulsively — coins, gems, interesting buttons, other people's valuables.
personality.ideals: Freedom. Rules are for people who lack the imagination to find a better way. I steal because property is a polite fiction, and I lie because truth is overrated. But I never steal from those who can't afford it, and I never lie to people I genuinely like.
personality.bonds: I stole a fey music box from a traveling merchant three months ago. It plays a haunting tune I can't get out of my head, and it pulled me toward the looking glass like a compass needle. Wonderland wants its trinket back — and I'm starting to think I was meant to bring it. Also, Poe is not just a familiar — he's the only friend I've never betrayed.
personality.flaws: I cannot resist stealing things, even when stealing them is monumentally stupid. I also have a pathological need to be the cleverest person in any room, and Wonderland — where cleverness is currency — is either the best or worst possible place for me. I trust no one fully and push people away with humor before they can get close enough to hurt me.

appearance: A lean, sharp-featured tiefling standing 5'10" with dusky red skin, swept-back horns that curve like a ram's, and a long, prehensile tail that moves expressively (and pickpockets independently when he's not paying attention). His eyes are solid amber with no visible pupils, giving him a perpetually calculating look. His black hair is cut short and artfully tousled, and a thin goatee frames a mouth that defaults to a knowing smirk. He wears well-tailored studded leather armor in black and dark crimson, designed to look like fashionable clothing from a distance. A raven named Poe perches on his shoulder — the familiar is unusually large and has an unsettling habit of tilting its head at people as though evaluating their net worth. Corvus moves with the easy, fluid grace of someone who has spent his life slipping through crowds, picking locks, and climbing walls. He keeps his hands in constant motion — shuffling cards, spinning coins, or gesturing while he talks — a habit that is both nervous tic and professional distraction.
backstory: Corvus Blackwood never knew his parents and doesn't particularly care to. He was raised in an orphanage in a large city, where he discovered early that a tiefling child's best survival tools were quick hands, a silver tongue, and an absolute lack of scruples. He ran away at twelve, fell in with a thieves' guild, and proved to be an exceptional con artist and burglar — charming, adaptable, and possessed of an almost supernatural ability to be somewhere else when things went wrong. He was also, despite his best efforts, not entirely heartless. He stole from the wealthy and occasionally, accidentally, helped people along the way. His familiar Poe — a raven he summoned during his first experiments with the arcane — became his constant companion and only genuine emotional attachment. Three months ago, Corvus lifted a music box from a traveling merchant's cart during a rain-soaked market day. The box was small, ornate, and clearly valuable — exactly his type of score. But when he opened it, the tune it played was unlike anything he'd ever heard: beautiful, strange, and aching with a melancholy that made his chest tight. Worse, he couldn't sell it. Every time he tried, his hands refused to let it go. The music box began to pull him — literally, physically — toward a ruined wizard's tower on the edge of town. He followed, because curiosity has always been his greatest flaw, and found a glowing looking glass that yanked him through into Wonderland. Now he's trapped in a world of mad logic and impossible rules, carrying a music box that hums with contentment, and slowly realizing that the box didn't choose him randomly — Wonderland needed a thief. Someone who breaks rules for a living. Someone who can steal a crown.
